title: Permutations
keyIdea: Decide position index: swap each candidate from index onward into it, recurse for index + 1, then swap back. At index == n the array is one permutation.

approaches.name: Swap, nums passed by value
approaches.idea: Same recursion, but each call gets its own copy of nums, so no swap back is needed.
approaches.why: Same number of calls, plus an O(n) copy per call.

approaches.name: Swap and swap back
approaches.idea: for i from index: swap(index, i), recurse(index + 1), swap(index, i) back.
approaches.why: n! permutations, each copied once into the answer.

quiz.q: Why swap back after the recursive call?
options: nums is shared by reference; the next choice must start from the unchanged array

quiz.q: Why does the pass-by-value version work without swapping back?
options: Each call works on its own copy, so a child never changes the caller's array

quiz.q: How many permutations does an array of n distinct numbers have?
What does index mean in recurPermute(index)?
options: The position being decided; everything before it is fixed
